newsitem.title: POLAND: Bad loans to pull down Slaski net in '97.
newsitem.headline: Bad loans to pull down Slaski net in '97.

text.p: Bank Slaski SA's 1997 net profit is likely to be lower than in 1996, when it reached 298 million zlotys, due to bad loans, its president said on Wednesday.
"We are all aware that it will be difficult to repeat last year's results, considering results in the first quarter," Brunon Bartkiewicz told a news conference.
The bank netted 47 million zlotys in the first quarter, down from about 100 million zlotys in the same period of 1996.
Bartkiewicz said the first quarter's profit fell, because the bank had to earmark 22 million for reserves on consumer credits.
"We think that what happened in the first quarter is a symptom of deteriorating consumption credit repayment and that is why we decided to create reserves," he said.
He said the bank was the creditor for some 250,000 people, who owed it about 700 million zlotys.
